title: Move the runtime without changing the trading lesson
purpose: An application that works on Compose still needs service discovery, readiness and ingress when moved to a cluster. This chapter is for developers learning Kubernetes through a familiar workload: keep the order workflow fixed while investigating its new runtime boundaries.
entryAssumptions: C2 combines orders, pricing and observability on Compose.
concepts: A pod is a scheduling unit. A Service gives stable routing to selected pods. Readiness determines whether a pod should receive traffic; replicas alone do not make a workflow correct.
runtimePrerequisites: Use the state quickstart for tool versions, generation, start and stop commands. Run one local state at a time because ports and generated output directories are shared.

transitions.carriesForward: Introduce limit orders, matching and fills while keeping orders distinct from executed trades.
transitions.motivation: C2 combines orders, pricing and observability on Compose.
transitions.increment: Run C2 on Kubernetes and explain ingress, service routing and pod readiness.
transitions.evidence: Runtime objects replace Compose placement while the order lifecycle remains. The namespace and service selectors explain where traffic goes. An unready backend and a missing ingress route require different fixes. Healthy pods alone do not establish working end-to-end routing.

before: C2 combines orders, pricing and observability on Compose.
after: Run C2 on Kubernetes and explain ingress, service routing and pod readiness.

objectives.outcome: Map an ingress request through a Kubernetes Service to ready pods and verify the retained order behavior.
Explain the evidence boundary: An unready backend and a missing ingress route require different fixes. Healthy pods alone do not establish working end-to-end routing.

walkthrough.action: Follow the kind quickstart, including the wait-ready status command and smoke test. Use kubectl get pods,svc -n traderx to map one trade request from ingress to its backend. Submit a small order through the UI and compare with C2 behavior.
walkthrough.expected: Runtime objects replace Compose placement while the order lifecycle remains. The namespace and service selectors explain where traffic goes.

walkthrough.action: Inspect kubectl describe pod for a service that is starting or unready, or inspect its readiness probe definition when all pods are ready. Compare process state with the readiness condition before diagnosing ingress.
walkthrough.expected: An unready backend and a missing ingress route require different fixes. Healthy pods alone do not establish working end-to-end routing.

assessments.question: Which observations separate a scheduling problem from an application routing problem?
assessments.guidance: Use pod events/readiness and Service endpoints, then test ingress and the business result. Explain which boundary each observation tests.

limitations: An unready backend and a missing ingress route require different fixes. Healthy pods alone do not establish working end-to-end routing.
This is an educational local demonstration. Passing its checks does not establish production readiness, financial settlement, or correctness under every failure mode.
